label: 🪶 테르메 보테 — 40대 앉은 비틀기
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, full body shot.
Model: one woman in her forties, full hourglass figure, soft strong build with a sharply defined waist, black hair in a low chignon.
Pose: seated on a low bench, hips angled to one side, torso twisting back so the chest turns toward the camera and reads frontal, one hand planted on the bench behind her, the other resting on the thigh, spine long, chin level.

Body fully painted with: Persian termeh weaving — the entire body covered in a continuous allover boteh paisley field with no plain ground anywhere. Curved teardrop boteh forms in jewel tones — garnet, lapis, emerald, saffron — each outlined in fine gold and filled with dense interior floral scrollwork, nested tightly so every boteh touches its neighbours. Tiny stem-and-leaf fillers occupy any remaining space. Uniform scale and density across chest, torso, arms and legs — no panels, no borders, no garment shape.

Pigment applied directly on bare skin, matte, pores and skin texture visible.
The paint ends at the wrist and ankle in ONE thin crisp border; hands and feet bare.
Hands fully visible, five separated fingers each. Nails medium almond-shaped, lacquered deep garnet.

Footwear: garnet-red satin platform stiletto sandals, 3cm platform, open toe with painted toenails visible.
Environment: a dark studio, one antique termeh panel mounted behind.
Lighting: warm key from the front left at 45 degrees, low and directional so the gold outlines flare along the chest and thigh, deep falloff behind.
Style: high fashion editorial meeting textile craft. ultra-sharp 8K. portrait 2:3 vertical.
